standard_prerequisites.name: Vanishing of cohomology of the members of the system on the objects of B
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, hypotheses (2) and (3) of the statement and the criterion relating the cohomology of a limit to the limit of the cohomologies
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the two vanishing statements that make the limit exact.

core_obligations: Show the limit is exact (proof lines 5262-5270): under hypotheses (2) and (3) the standard exact sequence relating the derived limit to the inverse limit has vanishing extra terms, so R lim F_n = lim F_n.
Vanishing of the cohomology (proof lines 5270-5276): the same exact sequence and hypothesis (2) give the vanishing of H^p(U, lim F_n) for p greater than zero and U in B.
proof_roadmap: Use the exact sequence of the derived limit to identify it with the ordinary limit.
Use hypothesis (2) to obtain the vanishing of the cohomology of the limit on B.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that under the hypotheses that the members of an inverse system of modules are acyclic on the objects of a covering family B and that the systems of sections have vanishing R^1 lim, the derived limit coincides with the ordinary inverse limit and the limit is acyclic in positive degrees on B (statement lines 5246-5260). The proof uses the exact sequence relating the derived limit to the limit and R^1 lim to identify the two (proof lines 5262-5270) and then reads off the vanishing (proof lines 5270-5276). The non-formal content is the reading of the hypotheses in that exact sequence. The claim is H2: one exact sequence plus two vanishing inputs.
